markdown: ## Watchlist - **BNP Paribas:** Fitch has cut BNP's outlook to negative because of France [Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxOSTFkajRXVHlWdlV1Mmt1OXJvYWM2Q0hzY0ZFdThCUjVIWWE1UjlaeWduZXJDMlpTOTBEMkN0d2lPTHV3V3NpUFhkRnJJbDNBQnNKdFBTWHRjbkJKeUJaTElBOWJJd2pGMWwtcHZfYXJFZU42VHBRNUpGUGdVdlNaQ3VqRU95bHdJZGhJa0hZVHBYd2R3X3ZXWVExOUpkSkhQYkNELVBrN21TaUxfakdVNFNNbw?oc=5). Credit Agricole got the same cut. The rating is unchanged for now, but check counterparty limits and how much euro cash sits with French banks. - **HSBC, JPMorgan:** Both are offering to help development banks get capital relief [Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxPLU91VjRabUZJWEYzV0tvOEdwQ2FFOXQ3TEc3R1R1R0ZJVGVHZVFWWG9CZWhKYjJ1WUxmUmwwVDNUdXBFbkxPOTduNVRZYUk2T1VpaDByWnplRnhCMDcwMk1ZVVlDeXRvQjFnemFkRlJSOWpMb2lpVFQ3OFpBaVZxajgxM0w0UU9Gb25aVDliSVJTOG0xZHZRbXZLUUlfQ3RwbFo2NlJ1NlIybGgwbWY4VkRmREgyQQ?oc=5). It is a strategic use of their balance sheets that could shape how much capacity they have for corporate lending. ## The brief - **Euro-zone inflation hit 4% in October, double the ECB's target and the highest in three years** [Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxOb3Jzd3dqaEhsS2REM3M2by1MU3hiZUIxbnRCYW1zR1NZSFg2YWJYblNxWERYeWFvMVRjZzNDNnFVR0RRZl9QdlQ2aG00TlVoM1pibEJiVHZPOERDRUlPM1pxcmFtV01YMUZrVHQ0dEEzRUEyVmF5bUxXNFE4UDBRWkZVanpoZnlKRFRTVzhNbVZNNVRyVk1mY0dnY1FsMmxPbUxBSXlrdUFOWGJqYVE?oc=5)[CNBC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxPZE40ZWZuWllSbGhUMVRQLVVNaU5lc1NVWnhZZFFRQWRDbTN1aDllekVocUlJTmZWUi1adGNVdFI5dVlGQ0xNWW9HZGVpanlqVjA2VWxlMFF2elgwWUd6T09hbHhaMTBRRlZzc1RwRVd0Tkc1Q1loZDVkYXpqTkYwY1F1dGxTYzlhZkE?oc=5). A December ECB hike now looks more likely, so expect higher euro deposit yields and higher EUR borrowing costs. - **Democrats swept the US midterms, and markets read it as a return towards normality** [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/fc404189-8dde-4dfe-8da7-0df8e92effd2?syn-25a6b1a6=1). More restraints on the administration could mean more predictable tariff policy, which matters for sourcing and pricing plans. - **Oil fell below $100 on hopes of peace after the election** [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/b526f876-810a-4e74-8b8d-4ffca04b29c7?syn-25a6b1a6=1). Cheaper fuel eases freight and input costs, which the ISM services survey has flagged alongside tariffs as a drag [CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/services-sector-growth-slows-impeded-tariffs-rising-fuel-costs-ism-inflation-fed-ai-trump/873799/). - **China blocked SoftBank's $5.4bn takeover of ABB's robotics division** [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/f10c3e24-45e4-47ff-bde2-24a8de90aec4?syn-25a6b1a6=1). The unit is focused on China and has a mega-factory in Pudong, so the block shows Beijing can veto deals involving industrial assets based in China. ## Rates & FX - **USD.** The dollar weakened sharply. EUR/USD rose 0.79% to 1.1267 (+1.2% on the week), and GBP/USD rose 0.66% to 1.35 (+1.6% on the week). This lifts the dollar value of European earnings and cash, and raises the cost of any open short-EUR hedges. - **Treasuries.** Yields fell, with the 2-year at 4.58% (-3bp) and the 10-year at 4.90% (-5bp, -15bp on the week). Lower long-end yields help any plans to issue or refinance term debt. SOFR is 3.97%. - **Bank of England today at 12:00 Dublin.** A hike to 4.00% from 3.75% is forecast on a 7-0-2 vote, and Bailey speaks at 12:30. A hike would lift returns on sterling cash and SONIA-linked borrowing costs. A surprise hold would weaken sterling. - **Other currencies.** €STR is 2.445%. EUR/GBP is 0.8346, USD/CNY is flat at 6.6723, and USD/MXN rose 0.26% to 18.646. US payrolls are due on Friday, forecast at 65K. ## Also worth knowing - **The European Payments Council has updated its Verification of Payee matching rules** for character handling and name checks [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48697/epc-publishes-new-verification-of-payee-matching-recommendations?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed). Expect changes in how euro payments are screened before they are released. - **Stanley Black & Decker raised its EPS outlook thanks to tariff refunds** [CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/stanley-black-decker-raises-outlook-tariff-refunds-boost-margins/873805/). It is pulling forward $70m to $80m of 2027 growth investment. - **Solvay struck a rare-earths deal using supply from a Brazilian mine** [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/7479802b-7071-4ab7-a7a0-bbebc20010e3?syn-25a6b1a6=1). The aim is to reduce dependence on China for magnets made in Europe and the US. - **Block reached a $964m settlement with the US Justice Department** [Payments Dive](https://www.paymentsdive.com/news/block-reaches-964m-doj-pact/873729/), most of it over an ineffective anti-money-laundering programme. ## Worth thinking about Euro inflation is at 4%, the dollar is falling and markets expect a December ECB hike. This is a good moment to review the EUR hedge ratio and to decide whether euro surplus cash should be locked into term deposits now. A related question for the team: if French bank ratings come under pressure, which non-French counterparties would take the euro deposits?
